clue.text: Speed and power associated with successful service

parts.note: in tennis an ace is a serve the receiver cannot touch

explanation.surface: A tennis commentator praises a player's fast, powerful serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace is the rate of movement, a synonym of velocity.

clue.text: Stick and whip will do for this animal

parts.note: a pole is a long stick
the cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip

explanation.surface: Someone advises a stick and whip for driving some beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will do for' sounds like 'will be enough to handle' but just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a small carnivorous mammal of the weasel family, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Singers having work reduced when one's brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the letter for one is placed inside the shortened word
reduced means the word for work is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a chore is a piece of work
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Choristers find their workload eased whenever an extra member joins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims CHORE to CHOR; 'brought in' puts I inside it before the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a group of vocalists performing together.

clue.text: Start to poke with stick?

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the word poke is taken

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A question about whether jabbing with a stick is the way to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: P begins 'poke', ROD is a stick, and to prod is to poke with one.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to jab at something, typically with a pointed implement.

clue.text: Some bridge that's liable to bend?

definitions.meaning: in the card game bridge, a set of games won by the first side to take two
a flexible elastic material, or something made of it, gives under pressure

explanation.surface: Asking whether part of a bridge might flex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' looks like a structure over a river but is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a rubber is a best-of-three match; the elastic substance bends easily.

clue.text: Show end of world is nigh

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word world is used

parts.note: nigh means near, close

explanation.surface: A doomsday preacher's placard announcing the world's end is near.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to reveal or make it known.

clue.text: Inclination to hear this composer

indicators.note: to hear means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A preference for listening to a certain composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' looks like a taste for the music but means a ship's tilt, a LIST, which is said like the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and pianist.

clue.text: Refrain from unnecessary tinkering and get water from tap?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for not meddling with something that works
read literally, stop using the well and draw water from the tap instead

explanation.surface: Advice not to meddle, and a householder switching to mains water.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: abandon the well as a water source because the tap supplies it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to avoid interfering with something satisfactory as it stands.

clue.text: Review of topic aims to be congenial

indicators.note: a review goes over material again, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic hopes that going over certain subjects will make things friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico describes someone likeable and easy to get along with.

clue.text: Give a roasting to right-winger throttling referee

indicators.note: throttling means the conservative's letters close around the referee's like hands round a neck

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A political supporter strangles an official and gets savaged for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a roasting to' suggests criticism but is meant literally: to torrefy is to dry or parch by heat.
explanation.definitionFit: To torrefy is to scorch or dry by fire, as with coffee beans.

clue.text: Like pay rises for all — or just the directors?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for applying to everyone equally
read literally, spanning only the board of directors

explanation.surface: Asking whether a pay increase is for every worker or only management.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'the board' as a company's board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a measure applied uniformly to every member of a group.

clue.text: One performing in dodgy club needed a little bit of pride?

indicators.note: in means the two short pieces go inside the jumbled letters
dodgy means unreliable, so the letters of club are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A performer in a shady nightclub needed some self-respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges the word club to LCUB, and 'in' places the two short pieces after its L. 'Pride' is a group of lions, not self-respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a group of lions, so its young member is a small part of it.

clue.text: Prison's severe critic

definitions.meaning: someone who slams, or harshly criticises, things

explanation.surface: A jail is described as a harsh judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a jail, and literally one who criticises harshly.

clue.text: Pink around opening in surface of body

indicators.note: around means the colour word encloses the word for a small opening

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour
a pore is a tiny opening in a skin or surface

explanation.surface: Describing pink flesh around a pore on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means relating to the physical, bodily frame.

clue.text: English short story about to lift one's spirits

indicators.note: about means the pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a tale is a short story

explanation.surface: An English short story that raises the reader's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns E plus TALE back to front, giving ELATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to make someone happy and excited.

clue.text: Hide most of the spots

indicators.note: most of means the word the loses its last letter

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Concealing the majority of pimples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb for concealing, but it means to beat, as in tanning someone's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide someone is to beat them, a sense shared with flog or thrash.

clue.text: Quickly get to tennis player that's become exhausted

parts.note: to run is to go quickly
a seed is a ranked tennis player in a tournament draw

explanation.surface: Rushing to reach a tennis star who has tired out.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that runs to seed has passed its best, so the idiom means to deteriorate or wear out.

clue.text: Harshness? It pays off when imprisoning monarch

indicators.note: imprisoning means the jumbled letters hold the monarch's letters inside them
off means wrong, so the letters of it pays are rearranged

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen

explanation.surface: Sternness pays dividends when jailing a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the words it pays into ASPITY, and 'imprisoning' sets the Queen's letters inside it, which ER is a crossword convention for.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is roughness or severity of manner.

clue.text: Avoid arrogance and upset feelings of offence

parts.note: side is an old word for pretentious, arrogant airs

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned over and read upwards

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or pique, as in 'in a pet'

explanation.surface: Steering clear of conceit and hurting people's feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PETS into STEP. SIDE meaning swagger is British.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep is to dodge or evade something.

clue.text: German author I encountered in border city on Rhine

parts.note: Thomas Mann was a German novelist

indicators.note: encountered in means the letter I is met within the word for a border

parts.note: a hem is the border of a cloth

explanation.surface: Meeting a German writer in a frontier town on the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Mannheim is a German city standing where the Neckar meets the Rhine.

clue.text: Rodents around plunder a possible cause of disease

indicators.note: around means the rodents' word encloses the word for plunder

parts.note: mice are rodents
to rob is to plunder

explanation.surface: Rats and mice raiding stores may spread illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbe is a microorganism, some kinds of which are germs causing illness.

clue.text: Having everyone striking with maximum effort

definitions.meaning: every worker is out on strike

explanation.surface: A total strike pursued with full commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: A total walkout calls everyone out; an all-out effort holds nothing back.

clue.text: Ray drank nothing, after swallowing first of rum

indicators.note: swallowing means the drinking word takes in the first letter of rum

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the word rum is used

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man called Ray stayed teetotal after downing a slug of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name but is the fish: the torpedo ray gives electric shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The torpedo is an electric ray, a flat fish.

clue.text: Frozen area with rocks on top

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds, as are rocks
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: An icy region with boulders lying above it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent sheet of ice covering polar land.

clue.text: Nothing found in search of hollow

indicators.note: found in means the letter for nothing is placed inside the searching word

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Searching for a hollow and finding nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: COOMB, also spelt combe, is a short valley in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb is a small valley or dip in hillside.

clue.text: Powered flight

parts.note: suggests aeroplanes, but means a flight of stairs moved by a motor

explanation.surface: Aviation driven by engines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' means a run of steps, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase is a flight of steps driven by a motor.

clue.text: Amount of heat obtainable from hydrogen in time

indicators.note: in means the hydrogen symbol is placed inside the word for time

parts.note: a term is a period of time
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Energy that hydrogen yields over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: A therm is a British unit of gas heat, 100,000 British thermal units.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat energy used in gas billing.

clue.text: A work such as Parsifal (not forgetting the Ring) may be effective

parts.note: Parsifal is Wagner's last opera

indicators.note: forgetting means the ring-shaped letter is dropped from the word not

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Wagner's Parsifal, and his Ring cycle too, may make an impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Ring' suggests Wagner's Ring cycle, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant means producing results, in operation.

clue.text: Summon witches, absorbing new energy

indicators.note: absorbing means the witches' group takes the letter for new inside it

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Calling up a group of witches, who draw in fresh power.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to call people together for a meeting.

clue.text: Inclined to take time off, so axed

indicators.note: to take off means the letter for time is removed from the word
off completes the phrase take off, which signals removal

parts.note: tended means inclined

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to take a break, so got the chop.
explanation.definitionFit: Axed means terminated or stopped, as is something finished.

clue.text: Wind instrument and piano that's interrupted by another

parts.note: P (piano) means soft in music

indicators.note: interrupted by means a second letter breaks into the abbreviation for that is

parts.note: ie (id est) means that is
another piano, so a second P

explanation.surface: A wind instrument and a keyboard, interrupted by a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is 'that is', i.e., which 'interrupted by' splits with another P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a simple tube blown to make music.

clue.text: What's fired a male meeting maiden? Love

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man meets a young woman and finds love.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo, short for ammunition, is what guns discharge.
